utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated and have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, has someone gone to get the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning to the interpreters. Does everybody hear me? General, do you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We will move through this document quickly, Mr. President. I don't think that on the 498 document, that we were discussing yesterday, we will submit the exhibits that we have tabbed there with our chart for the Court's review, and that being the receipt that is in tab number 1 on 498, as well as, the orders that are listed in this binder from tab 2 through 11, and their corresponding Defence numbers. The ones provided by Mr. Primorac have no numbers, the ones introduced by the Defence do, in fact, have numbers. We direct the Court's attention to tab 12, which is the letter of Mr. Blewitt, the Deputy Prosecutor, to Mr. Primorac asking for the source of these documents, and for the originals. Mr. Primorac responded in document 13 in that response to Mr. Blewitt. He reflected that he received these documents from an individual by the name of Jure Brkic and that he never possessed the originals. Tab 14, Mr. President, is the establishment by the Narodni Lists or the official Gazette of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna to establish the war archive. Tab 15 is the decision appointing a director of the war archive by the name of Stjepan Ivankovic and tab 16 is the appointment of Mr. Jure Brkic as the deputy director of the war archive, that is the person from whom Major General Primorac says he got these documents. Now, if I may, Mr. President, as the Court knows in the issue of binding orders by this Court, a binding order was issued by this Court and I would like, at this point, to address my attention and the attention of the witness to two particular documents and/or orders that have been issued by the federation in the Ministry of Defence pursuant to this Court's orders. And if I may take those in series.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What order are you talking about Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm about to give it to the usher, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ordinarily orders are covered by either ex parte or by closed sessions. Do you want this to still be a public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have no objection one way or the other Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you have no objection, we can remain in public hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me consult with my colleagues on this point, but I don't think there is any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We would just like to get a question to the witness, Mr. President. We have been in session now for five minutes, we haven't had a question put to the witness yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just wait a minute Mr. Hayman. You know that in this Tribunal everybody takes his time. You were the first to do so, in fact, when the witness answers the Prosecution's questions. But, I will ensure that the questions are asked. Have faith in me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, and if I can. INTERPRETER: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, and if I may give these particular documents, the first one, which is dated the 28th of February, 1997, signed by Mr. Ante Jelavic and there are English and BCS copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: These are documents that you are giving to the witness in order to cross-examine him --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: -- or you simply want to open a discussion. Very well. All right, you see, Mr. Hayman, the questions will be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this discussion of the binding order is absolutely outside of the scope of these proceedings, but I trust that you will reach the right decision on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have to wait to see what kind of questions are going to be asked in order to decide whether what you said is right. The witness, thanks to you, in the first place, covered so many issues, that are at the very core of this trial, that you cannot limit the cross-examination, although I am watching to hear what is being asked. Let's wait for the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 499, 499A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, I will give you a moment to review that document, sir. We are talking about the document signed by Mr. Jelavic on the 28th of February, 1997?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could I have a translation, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this particular document has not been translated yet into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, I understand. I'm not trying to interrupt things. I would like you to read it quickly so the interpreters can interpret it, and I don't lose any of the meanings. I see, generally, what it's about, but I would prefer to have it read so I can understand all nuances. Why don't you begin with pursuant to articles 27. Don't read the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. "Pursuant to articles 27 and 28 of the law on defence of the BH Federation, official Gazette of the BH Federation, issue 1596, in order to provide, and in order to provide complete protection of the records and archives, I hereby order that: 1. The commanders of the Operative Zones subordinate units, administrations and institutions of the HVO to gather and catalogue all available archives pertaining to the war for the homeland in their zone of responsibility. Prior shall be given to the period between 1 April, 1992 and 1 January, 1994. 2. The gathered material shall be urgently forwarded to the Croatian Defence Council offices in Mostar by 15 March, 1997. 3. The commanders mentioned under paragraph 1 of this order shall be responsible to me for the execution of this order. Copies going to the HVO command, HVO Operative Zones, all HVO subordinate units, all HVO administrations, all, and files, and it is signed by the Defence minister, Ante Jelavic." Now, my question, Brigadier, with regard to this document was, did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember such a document, but as far as I can recall, I believe that this is the signature of the Defence minister, Mr. Jelavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, what position did you hold on the 28th of February, 1997?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 28 February, 1997, I was on duty in Tomislavgrad as chief of staff, and in this period for which the documents are sought, the period between 1 April, 1992 and 1 January, 1994, I was on duty in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular order, and to whom it's directed, would cover the command in which you were working in Tomislavgrad on the 28th of February, 1997; would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This order was central commands and I was in the command in Tomislavgrad, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about this order, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding this order and the tasks that it sets out, in Tomislavgrad command, I have not, I did not hear of it, and I never saw it, even though I was on such a post that the commander would have had to notify me of it, because here it is clear that the document is going directly to all the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me, Brigadier, turn your attention to another document with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 500, 500A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, if you could review that document for us, Exhibit 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission I will read this document again, starting with the date of 4 March, 1997 and again starting pursuant to article 27 and 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The date is 4 March, 1997, "Pursuant to articles 27 and 28 of the law on defence of the BH Federation, citing the Official Gazette, and in order to provide complete protection of the records and archives, I hereby order that: 1. You protect against damage, destruction, removal and relocation all archives gathered, as stipulated in the order reference number 01-112/97 of 28 February, 1997. 2. The commanders of Operative Zones, subordinate units, administrations and institutions of the HVO shall be responsible to me for the execution of the task under paragraph 1 of this order. Copies: HVO command, HVO operative zones, all; HVO subordinate units, all; HVO administrations, all; and files." Again, signed by the Defence minister, Ante Jelavic. Brigadier, again, that is Mr. Jelavic's signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This signature is identical to the signature on the other order, and I think I said as far as I know that this is the signature of Mr. Ante Jelavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, the reference number of 01-112/97 is the number in the prior order, Exhibit 499.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, Brigadier, you were in the Tomislavgrad headquarters on the 4th of March, 1997?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in command in Tomislavgrad. Let me repeat, the documents which have been produced, that is, the time frame within which these were produced, I was not in the command of Tomislavgrad, I was in the command in Vitez in the pertinent time period. I am just trying to understand why I am not aware of these documents. It could be that this is why I did not learn of them, because these documents may have been produced at a time when I was not present at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, you, in the command, would have been covered by the copies, and your command would have received a copy of this order; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but from the first document, you can see that it was addressed to the commanders, and it was specifically addressed to all the commanders. So, the commander who was there in Tomislavgrad, if he had received this document, he acted accordingly, to the best understanding of what he was supposed to do. During that period, during the time frame which is referred to in the document, I was not present there; so, maybe that was the reason why I was not included, I was not let known of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, this exhibit, this order on the 4th of March, 1997, have you ever seen this before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I have not seen this document, either. Because this document is linked to the previous document. So, had I seen the previous document, or had I seen this document, I would have looked up the previous document, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be accurate to say that you haven't heard about it, either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not heard of the document, per se, but I did see, in the command, that there was some work done, some archival work; that is, the officers who were in charge of the archives. I'm aware of the fact that certain things were classified. Now, what was being done, how it was classified, that, I don't know, because I was not working at the Tomislavgrad command. Had I been in Vitez, then obviously I would have been involved and I would have known what was done, because I worked with all these documents while I was in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, when you saw these people gathering archival material in the Tomislavgrad headquarters, did you ask them what they were doing and why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me be accurate. These were not people. There is an office, general services, and this is what is being done there on a regular basis. It wasn't something extraordinary. There were certain premises where these documents, all the documents which were produced there, was being stored and put in archive. It wasn't a special type of activity that was involved in classifying and archiving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, what you observed was people in the headquarters going about their normal course of business; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just for clarity sake, Mr. President, so we can distinguish between these two sets, the documents received in 499 and 500, the two we just discussed, those were the documents that were issued subsequent to the binding order or subpoena litigation. I just want to clarify that. In 498, the documents with the orders were documents received by the Office of the Prosecutor in a request for assistance by the Office of the Prosecutor. So, just for the clarity of the record, and any inaccuracies, I just wanted to segregate those two aspects of these documents. I will move on to another subject. Excuse me a moment. I have just one further clarification: On these two orders, 500 and 499, Mr. Harmon informs me that they were issued pursuant to the subpoena and not the binding order litigation. So, it was pursuant to the subpoena. So, to be perfectly clear as to where these documents follow-up in the sequence of the litigation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What's the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The date of these two orders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, the order. What was the date of the order you're talking about, so I can remember what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, consult with Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, the subpoena was the one from Judge McDonald; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So, it was January of 1997; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was actually, the specific date, Mr. President, is the 28th of February, 1997. I'm sorry, the date of the subpoena is the 17th of January, 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, it was January.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It seemed to me it was January. All right, January, 17 January, 1997. So, that was further to the -- the order is further to the -- from the Appeals Chamber, about five months later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon informs me that it was before that. Mr. Harmon conducted this litigation, if you want further explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, I don't need any further explanation about that. All right, perhaps after these clarifications, perhaps we could go back to substantive questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, before we move into a new subject, which we will do shortly, I just want to recall you back to an exhibit we discussed yesterday. And if I could show that you exhibit again, which is 456/65.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just move that down a little bit, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is the order that we discussed yesterday concerning Ivica Bagaric, and you said that Mr. Bagaric had no troops, soldiers under his command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivica Bagaric, while acting as chief of the anti-air defences, did not have a commanding function. That position is not a commanding function, it is an expert position, just as when I was head of the operations and training department. I didn't have a command function.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you a document, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 501, 501A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, is that Colonel Blaskic's signature, or someone signing on his behalf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is, as far as I can recognise, a document signed by the Chief of Staff of the headquarters, Franjo Nakic, on behalf of Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that the stamp of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the stamp of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's read it quickly. 9th of January, 1993 at 10.45, and the subject is anti-aircraft defence units. "Attention: The Travnik Brigade. The chief of anti-aircraft defence, the commander of the 4th anti-aircraft defence, light artillery missile division. Order: All anti-aircraft defence weaponry on the Travnik defence line, including the 4th anti-aircraft defence light artillery missile division, 3rd platoon of the first battery, shall join the anti-aircraft defence units that form the HVO Brigade of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone, anti-aircraft defence, light artillery missile platoon and the anti-aircraft defence platoon of the manoeuvring battalion. 2. Mr. Ivica Bagaric, chief of the anti-aircraft defence brigade, shall select and train troops on the weaponry that are at the brigade's disposal." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is because of the translation that I'm standing up. Point 2 has been misinterpreted. Ivica Bagaric is not chief of the anti-aircraft brigade, but he is chief of anti-aircraft defence. Ivica Bagaric is not a commander of a unit, but a chief of anti-aircraft defence. It is an error in the translation of point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm reading the translation that was given to us by the translation section. I don't pretend to read -- and if the interpreters can read it, if it can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The interpreters give us a translation Mr. Nobilo. Reread point 2 and we will ask our interpreters to be very careful as to what they are going to tell us, as they do always, but especially on this occasion. Oh, slowly, point 2, Mr. Ivica Bagaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. "The chief of anti-aircraft Defence of the brigade, Mr. Ivica Bagaric, shall select and train troops on the weaponry that are at the brigade's disposal." For the sake of clarification, reference is to the Travnik brigade, as can be seen from the whole text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In other words, if I understand you well, for the Prosecution, he is the chief of the anti-air defence brigade, and for the defence, he is head of the anti-aircraft defences at the level of the brigade. So this seems to me rather semantic. I must say I don't quite understand the distinction, but perhaps you could explain it to us, or maybe the witness could. As far as I'm concerned, if you are head of the anti-air defence at the level of the brigade, you do have command responsibilities. Perhaps it would be better to say chief of the anti-air defence brigade. But please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may make a suggestion. Not one of us is a soldier, but the witness is. Perhaps we could ask him because there are some abbreviations here that are not translated. The 4th LTRDPZO, that can be the key to everything so we avoid any guesswork.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before putting the question to the witness, I should like to hear the opinion of the Prosecutor regarding the translation that was given to us. We asked our interpreters for their expertise, so, Mr. Prosecutor, what do you think of it? And then we can go on to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think the accurate thing to do, Mr. President, is give the translation to the translation section, put it on the ELMO and have them translate it. I don't speak the language, Mr. President, and this is the interpretation that was provided upon submission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that perhaps, after all, this is not the most important thing. We must focus on what we are trying to see. The Prosecution is trying to show, I think, that Ivica Bagaric had troops under his orders whether he was chief of the anti-aircraft defence brigade or chief of the anti-aircraft defence at the level of the brigade. I would like to ask the Brigadier, according to this text, was Mr. Ivica Bagaric, should Mr. Ivica Bagaric, according to this order, select and train troops under his responsibility? What is your feeling, Brigadier? Will you please answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Ivica Bagaric was not in command of units. As chief of anti-air defences, chief of anti-air defences within a command, he is the most qualified person who should watch over the situation regarding units of the anti-air defences. So, between Ivica Bagaric and the anti-air defence units, there are commanders. These units are part of a brigade, like a battalion. The commanding role, or function, in every command, is in the hands of the commander only. All the others are associates, they make suggestions, express their opinions and pass expert decisions, but they cannot give orders. Therefore, Ivica Bagaric could never write an order and say "I hereby order." In the area of air defences, he could prepare a document, but the order will be issued by the commander. Why? Because that order is addressed to subordinate commanders, that is commanders of anti-air defence units. But he is an expert, he will go to the command and assist, but he cannot give orders to those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, you would agree with me that the order says that individuals shall join the anti-aircraft defence that form the HVO brigade; does it say that in the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me try to explain the first paragraph word-by-word, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but try and go a little more quickly, otherwise we will still be here in a month's time asking you questions about the brigade. But I remember that we had a chart, and under the orders of the accused there was an anti-air brigade. As far as I remember, Ivica Bagaric was mentioned, and he was at the same level at the other brigades. I would like this polemics to end rather quickly and the Judges will judge. Mr. Nobilo first, and then your comments, and then we will close this discussion; because otherwise we will never get out of it. Mr. Nobilo, quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I quite agree with you that this is not decisive for this case, but in this way our witness is trying to be impeached. But let us give the witness the chance to explain himself fully, because we wouldn't like his credibility to be called in question. As it has been opened to scrutiny, please let him explain himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But, Mr. Nobilo, the Brigadier is here before us. There is no need for -- he doesn't need your help. He's big enough to defend himself. So, if you need to comment on this, Brigadier, please do, but quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, when we are dealing with anti-air defence units in the Operative Zone Central Bosnia command, you noticed very well, Mr. President, that the commander of the Operative Zone had under his command a unit called the 4th LTRD, and it had its commander. It had its commander. Because of needs on the defence lines, all the weaponry from the brigades and from the 4th anti-aircraft defence light artillery missile division had to be collected together. As we're talking about the area of the Travnik Brigade, the qualified person for selecting those weapons is the chief of anti-air defences, Mr. Ivica Bagaric. In the command of the Operative Zone we also had a chief of anti-air defences, but we also had a commander. The same applies to the Travnik Brigade. In the brigade command, in addition to the commander, there are 15 other persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, we have more or less understood. One last question and then move forward, please, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last question on this, Brigadier. In addition to this, according to paragraph 2, there was training of these troops being done also; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The anti-air defence weaponry, because of their importance and use, training was carried out, so as to react as quickly as possible should the need arise for the personnel to be able to use these weapons. Because what else would they be doing except training for the use of these weapons, so, there was training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are going to go to another question. Let me summarise. Mr. Bagaric officially did not have troops under his command, but in view of this order, which is not challenged, he had the duty to select and train troops. The Court will judge on that basis. Please move forward, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, let's move to another section. You were asked some questions by Defence, my learned colleague, Mr. Nobilo, concerning the causes of the conflict between the Bosnian Muslims and the Bosnian Croats, and we're certainly not going to read everything that you stated at that point, which runs from page 12.240 to 12.245; but I would like to ask you a couple of follow-up questions about some of what you said and some of the documents that were introduced by the Defence. I would like to talk to you preliminarily about Defence Exhibit 199.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It was the first Defence exhibit, Mr. Kehoe, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think either the first or second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I just hope you won't have questions regarding all the exhibits that are going to come after this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that document, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You identified that document, and you discussed that document, and you pointed to number 1 in that document that was talking about the crisis headquarters being renamed the HVO command; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I identified this document by recognising General Blaskic's signature. It is clear, that at the time, General Blaskic was a commander in Kiseljak. In point one, the crisis headquarters is renamed the municipal command. Yes, that is the transformation. It is the first step towards reorganisation. It was first called a crisis headquarters, and then after a certain amount of time these municipal commands were established. So, that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, you said that the setting up of the municipal headquarters, the municipal HVO command, was one of the steps that Blaskic took in trying to organise the HVO; didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not quite what I said, because it wasn't possible under those conditions. I'll explain why. At the time General Blaskic was on duty in a municipality in May 1992, and the organisation of the municipal command followed the chain of command, probably it was called the main headquarters at the level of the HVO at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, you would agree with me, based on what you said in direct, that this was an effort by Blaskic to organise the HVO in Kiseljak. Didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is visible from this document that General Blaskic sought to establish the HVO in Kiseljak. I wish to draw attention to the heading of this document. It says that it came from a higher level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But today is Friday, let us make an effort to speed up the debate. I apologise for reminding you of this. Mr. Kehoe, when you show a document in the cross-examination to the witness, I would like to ask you to go directly to your question. We are not going to repeat all that has been confirmed by the witness. If that is being challenged, yes, then you can ask whether it was signed by Blaskic or not. This was a Defence exhibit. If you have one or two or three questions to put regarding this exhibit, please do so; because you know very well that the witness is very eloquent and he has many things to say, he is going to explain, going into a great deal of detail. After all, I am responsible for the scheduling and the work and the progress of this hearing. If there is something that is being contradicted, go to it immediately; if not, proceed to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I appreciate your point, Mr. President, and I will move as quickly as I possibly can. I would like the Brigadier to take a look at a series of documents, Prosecutor's documents, that are numbered 314, 315, 316, and 317, in series. If I can ask the Brigadier to keep Exhibit 199 with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, the first document is Exhibit 314, and it is signed by Josip Boro, the chairman of the crisis committee, and dated the 23rd of April, 1992. It says -- in Kiseljak -- it says, "On the basis of article 7 of the Kiseljak municipality statute," and it gives the number, "at its meeting held on the 23rd of April, 1992, the municipal crisis staff passed the following decision: The HVO headquarters for the area of Kiseljak municipality shall be formed. This decision comes into effect on the day of its proclamation." Exhibit 315, another document, very brief, signed by Mr. Josip Boro four days later, and it says: "Pursuant to the record, the hand over and acceptance of the barracks signed by the commander of the barracks, Ljuban Kosovac, and the chairman of the municipal crisis staff, Josip Boro, at its meeting on the 27th of April, 1997, the municipal crisis committee passed the following decision: The barracks in the Kiseljak municipality are handed over to be used and managed by the HVO headquarters of the Kiseljak municipality. This decision comes into effect on the day of its issue." I apologise for the dates going back, but this is the series that it went in, 316, another order on April the 24th, again by Mr. Boro, that appoints a commission for the building of the inventory list of weapons in the Kiseljak barracks, five individuals, both Muslims and Croats with the accused, Mr. Blaskic, on the list. The last in the series, on the 17th, there is a distribution, an agreement to distribute the weapons on a national representation. "The earlier distributed arms will be compensated by the commission mentioned earlier." Now the next document we have is the document that you talked about previously on the 10th of May, wherein Colonel Blaskic renames, or the crisis headquarters is renamed the municipal HVO staff. Let me show you a document that was issued the next day, the 11th May, 1992, and signed by the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 502 and 502A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Take a look at that document, Brigadier, and my first question: Is that the accused's signature on the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that this is the signature of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's read this document very briefly. Again, it's the 11th of May, 1992, the day after the document you said was setting up the HVO municipal headquarters in Kiseljak. "On the basis of the orders received from the main headquarters," and it gives a number of 10 April, 1992 and 8 May, 1992, "and with the intention of defining precisely the legal status of all formations, I am issuing the following order: 1. The only legal military units in the area of Kiseljak municipality are HVO units. 2. All other military units in the mentioned area must join the unified defence system and recognise the municipal HVO command as their main command. 3. Each member of the above mentioned military units is obliged to wear the HVO insignia, coat of arms on the cap, linen HVO sign on the left sleeve. 4. I forbid the establishment of private military units. Persons who do not obey this order or do not carry it out ... and it's illegible ... and the established formation militarily destroyed. 5. By this order, all orders of the Territorial Defence are rendered invalid and the Territorial Defence in this area considered illegal. All troops are to be formed into ranks and the deadline to form them into ranks is the 11th." This order, it clearly reflects that the only legal military units in the Kiseljak area is the HVO and the Territorial Defence is now an illegal entity; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that from the order. However, you can see that this document was drafted on the basis of the, another order by the main headquarters of the HVO. I was not in Kiseljak at that time. I do not know the circumstances under which this document was drafted, so I cannot speak to anything that is set out in this document. But I can say that it was drafted on the basis of another document, and I can refer you to the number and the date here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, you discussed with us your Defence Exhibit 199, which was issued one day before, and you explained what that document was, and I'm showing you a document one day after that, and my question for you is: Was the HVO taking over in the Kiseljak municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether the HVO had taken over Kiseljak. That was 11 May. This is the time when I was working in the defence office in Novi Travnik. There may be other things which may indicate what has transpired here, but I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a photograph that is photograph 80/7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could put that on the ELMO, Mr. Usher, and if we could push the ELMO closer to the Brigadier. Mr. Usher, the all too valuable chopstick is at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, taking a look at 80/9, you, of course, recognise Colonel Blaskic in that photograph; do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see a man by the name of Dario Kordic in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you take the pointer and point to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that this is Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would like you to take a look at the Prosecutor's Exhibit 208 at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Keep that handy, please. You don't have to necessarily leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, take a look at this document, Brigadier, and we can put that on the ELMO. This is a document that is received in evidence, signed by Mr. Kordic, and pardon my pronunciation, Ivo Brnada. Before we talk about this document, did Mr. Kordic visit the Hotel Vitez while you were working there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, in fact, I saw Mr. Kordic in the Hotel Vitez in 1992 at Christmas when there was a reception at the command. This was on Christmas Eve when Mr. Blaskic organised a party to celebrate Christmas. There were UNPROFOR representatives there, and I believe there were also the BH representatives there, and this was the first time that I saw Mr. Blaskic at the Operative Zone command. This was in the Vitez Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said Mr. Blaskic, I think you mean Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is when I first saw Mr. Kordic in the Operative Zone command. This was a celebration, a reception at Christmas. I attended it, there were political representatives present, representatives of UNPROFOR; and I am not sure about the BH army representatives, but I believe that they may have attended, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How often did you see him in the Hotel Vitez after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see Mr. Kordic very frequently in the Vitez Hotel. I have no information that he was a frequent visitor there. Let me just take you back to the word "frequently." To me frequent would mean once a week, once every ten days; so if I say he was not a frequent visitor, this is what I have in mind, 10, 15, 20 days. As far as I know, Mr. Kordic had his office in Busovaca, and I never was in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you would agree with me, Brigadier, that the photograph, 80/9 we just had on the ELMO, is a shot, that is a photograph, that is taken outside of the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will attempt to analyse this structure. I cannot say that this is in front of the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let's move on. How frequently did Blaskic appear in press conferences with Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is as far as I can recall, the press conferences were introduced at a time when we were completely surrounded, when we were completely isolated, and we did not have media outlets, radio, we did not have access to the Bosnian state television. The situation in the enclave where we lived was so complex, so difficult, that General Blaskic, Mr. Kordic as a politician, and I know that Mr. Ignac Kostroman also appeared at these press conferences; so, they would appear and they would answer questions by journalists regarding the issues which were then topical. Let me just give you an illustration of how difficult the situation was. I took the list of those killed in the Vitez municipality, and on average, about 60 people were dying in Vitez, and about 65 were injured or wounded. So that was the situation. Without the media and proper way of communication, I think, this is why the press conferences were instituted; and these were public events, so anybody could come and attend or have access to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, since this morning is long, perhaps we will take a 15 minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Have the accused brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, the question I asked you before the break was how often these press conferences were, and let me make it simple. These press conferences were weekly, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, but I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at photograph as well as the document 208, which is -- this is Prosecutor's 208, which is dated the same day as Defence 199, a document that you identified. Does the witness have photograph as well as the document 208? Now, Brigadier, this is a document in evidence, and you are certainly welcome to review it. This discusses, in the preparatory language, "In connection with the brutal armed attack by the so-called Busovaca Territorial Defence led by Dervis Sarajalic." In any event, let's look at some of the orders, and this is executed by Mr. Kordic and Mr. Brnada, and the order is: "1. The agreement between the HVO and the so-called Busovaca Territorial Defence on the distribution of weapons is hereby terminated, and it has been decided that the Busovaca HVO forces take over all weapons, equipment, material, as well as the barracks. "2. The town of Busovaca is to be completely blocked from all sides. "3. All paramilitary formations, the so-called Territorial Defence, individuals, and others are given the ultimatum to hand over all weapons in their possession by Sunday, 1200 hours, or place them under HVO command, which includes the wearing of HVO insignia." Again, you're welcome to read the entire document, but let's move quickly to 7. "7. The mobilisation of all Busovaca HVO forces is to be completed." And then down to 11. "11. The Municipal Crisis Committee is dismissed in accordance with the orders of the HVO of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna and the Busovaca HVO is to take over all authority." Now, based on the documents that you've seen in Kiseljak and in Busovaca, it would appear that the HVO is taking over power in both of those municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, whether this was so. Mr. President, Your Honours, the documents which we are reviewing now were drafted in the municipalities. I did not see these documents and I cannot comment on them. All I know about Busovaca in this time period -- and this is what I heard from the radio -- I know that there were certain incidents, I know that there were certain incidents -- and here I see that a member of the HVO was killed, and this was going on during the period when the former JNA barracks was being taken over, and this was all in connection with the take-over of the barracks which was a depot and by the distribution of the weapons there, and this is all I know about those events that you are referring to in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, you gave us a series and an explanation of the causes of the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats, and I'm going to ask you a series of questions on some of the documents in evidence in that particular subject area, and I turn your attention to the next photograph as well as the document 318, 319, 323, and 324 and 325. Once again, Mr. Dubuisson, that's 318, 323, 324, 325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is it a Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, it's a Prosecution Exhibit. I apologise. Mr. Dubuisson, after we discuss these documents, we'll move to Prosecutor's photograph as well as the document 209.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about these documents in a series, starting with the first one, 318, of the 12th of May, 1992. Now, on the 12th of May, 1992, again this is an order by Josip Boro, the Chairman of the Municipal Crisis Staff, and he orders or decides "that the complete manpower, material assets, and technical equipment of the reserve structure of the public security station are to be put at the disposal of the HVO." Now, this is one day after Blaskic's order outlawing the Territorial Defence and making the HVO the only legal military authority in Kiseljak; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot answer that this was so or that this was not so. The documents speak for themselves. Regarding the decisions which were adopted by the municipal leadership, this is the time when the republican authorities practically did not exist, and the municipal authorities, for all intents and purposes, took over those competencies. But I cannot say anything about Kiseljak and -- I was far away from it and the date is 12 May, 1992, so I am unable to answer you either in the affirmative or in the negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at photograph as well as the document 319, again another order from Mr. Boro in Kiseljak, this one dated the 25th of May, 1992, and again he's saying, "On the basis of the Statute of the Kiseljak municipality, on the 25th of May, 1992, it is decided with reference to the decree of the presidency number," and he talks about the particular number, "the Crisis Staff cancels the current account of the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence and declares the use of the seal of this body null and void." So by this order, approximately two weeks after Blaskic outlaws the Territorial Defence, the Municipal Staff of the HVO in Kiseljak cancels their bank account; is that right? Is that what the documents reflects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what is stated in this decision. Whether this actually happened, I do not know. But let me repeat, this document also speaks of the paralysis of the central authorities and the municipal authorities take over the competencies of the central government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's talk about photograph as well as the document 323, another order by the Municipal Crisis Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have an objection here, and this is just to rationalise these proceedings. He said that in May of 1992, he was not in Kiseljak; he does not know what went on there. But we have a whole series of documents regarding Kiseljak in that time period, and he had already initially stated that he was not there, that he did not know what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, what do you answer to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness gave us approximately six pages on the cause of the conflict between the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims. We are going through the virtual take-over of all of these municipalities in addition to the witness's municipality which we are going to get to very shortly. That's the first point. The second point is the document that the Defence put in, photograph as well as the document 199, which was a document that was described as Blaskic's efforts to organise the HVO, has to be seen in the context of what's happening in Kiseljak, and what's happening in Kiseljak is a complete take-over of Kiseljak by the HVO. The order that was put in by the Defence was followed by an order the next day by the accused outlawing the Territorial Defence. At the same time, what is taking place in Busovaca is a take-over of the Busovaca municipality by the HVO there. So certainly after the expansive testimony given by this witness at the behest of questioning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The witness's testimony covered a very broad period, including his own evaluation of the conflict's cause. I think the Prosecutor is using a legitimate method, even though it may appear long, even to me, but that is his method, and I think it is legitimate for him to ask these questions. But perhaps, Mr. Kehoe, you could go a little more directly to your question and present your objectives a bit more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, I would like you to take a look at a series of documents, and that is Prosecutor's Exhibit 323, 324, and 325. If you could give the witness those documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 323, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 323, 324, and 325. Mr. President, we will be talking about those in a series.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps what you should do, Mr. Kehoe, because I too am very worried, perhaps for different reasons from Mr. Nobilo's, but I'm very concerned about all the time that this is taking. When you say that you're going to bring in 323, 324, and 325, perhaps you could very quickly say that they concern this point, for example, Kiseljak or Busovaca, and that I suggest doing that, because it is true, it is taking a long time. That's my first comment. My second is that I am asking -- I know that it is very difficult for Mr. Dubuisson, but I would like him to remain as close as possible to the witness so that putting the documents on the ELMO will take as little time as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will go through these documents very quickly in accordance with your guidelines, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in photograph as well as the document 323, on the 15th of June of 1993, the Croatian dinar is introduced into Kiseljak as well as other currencies. Photograph as well as the document 324 orders that all pricing should be displayed in Croatian dinars in Kiseljak. Exhibit 325 is a decision on changing the name of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Kiseljak to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's how you should do it, yes. That way the witness will react to all of these considerations. Brigadier, you understood the question and you may answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The last document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the last document, the executive board in Kiseljak changes its name to the HVO, and it says that the HVO "shall consist of." Now, do you see those documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have the document before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were similar things taking place in your municipality, Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the formation of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, as far as I know, provisional regulations were passed to establish civilian organs of authority. I don't know the time, which forms of civilian bodies, but I cannot claim categorically whether, before those regulations were passed, any documents of this kind were passed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Will you please answer more directly, Brigadier? Of course, it is your fundamental right to make your comments, but in view of efficiency, when a question is rather simple, will you please say whether you had this or that, "Yes" or "No," in Travnik, so please try. When you need to make a comment that you consider to be especially important, the Judges will not prevent you from doing so, but let us try and focus on the essentials. Your next question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question simply is: Did the HVO attempt to take control of the Novi Travnik municipality during this time frame?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say that with certainty because I'm not quite fully familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us put photograph as well as the document 80/7 on the ELMO, and if photograph as well as the document 456/109 could be given to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is a Prosecution Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Mr. President. I neglected to say that both of those are Prosecution Exhibits, the photograph as well as the document 456/109.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Briefly, what are these exhibits about, please, while they're looking for them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The particular photograph is a photograph of the three individuals who operated in conjunction with the accused at a meeting in Busovaca that took place on the 22nd of September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. And 456/109?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, before we review the particular document, Brigadier, I would ask you to take a look at the photograph that's on the ELMO, and do you know the three men that are in camouflage uniforms, and using the pointer, can you identify the three of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, on this photograph I recognise two gentlemen in uniform, Mr. Ignac Kostroman and Mr. Dario Kordic. The third person I do not recognise, or at least I can't recognise him on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, maybe we will show you another photograph, 80/8. Do you recognise him in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one I didn't recognise in the previous photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct. Well, do you recognise the man that is the second from the left carrying the suitcase and dressed in a camouflage uniform with a moustache? Do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This gentleman?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do recognise him on this photograph. It is Mr. Anto Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Anto Valenta had an office at some point in the Hotel Vitez, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Anto Valenta did stay in an office in the Vitez Hotel. As far as I recalled, he had the position of vice-premier of the government of Herceg-Bosna. I know he was in the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let me turn your attention to Exhibit 456/109, which is an excerpt of the minutes of the meeting of the Croatian Defence Council in the municipalities of Central Bosnia dated 22 September, 1992. Now, Brigadier, the front page of that document reflects the working presidency as Dario Kordic, Anto Valenta, Tihomir Blaskic, and Ignac Kostroman. Do you see that on the front page of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk to -- under the sub-heading "Situations in Municipalities." In Novi Travnik, your municipality, the document reflects that "it is estimated that the HVO holds about 70 per cent of the authority while the Muslims hold about 30." Vitez: "There is still dual authority. There is a possibility of confrontation between the Croats and the Muslims because of the HVO's taking power." Let's turn the page, two pages, and go to Busovaca. Busovaca: "HVO authority was set up on 9 May, 1992. HVO is the only authority. However, the setting up of the Muslims People Council is a concern." Turn the page. Kiseljak. Kiseljak: "The HVO is in complete control. However, there are frequent conflicts with respect to the competencies of civilian and military authority. Almost all enterprises are working. Salaries are paid in Croatian dinar. After the conflict with the Muslims which was staged by the leaders from Sarajevo through Mujahedeen, the situation is quite stable. Military HVO authority is dominant." Now, these documents reflect the situation in Novi Travnik, Busovaca, Vitez, and Kiseljak, and this document reflects that the HVO has taken virtual control of all of those municipalities; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document reflects the situation in the municipalities you mentioned, but I cannot claim that power has been taken over because it is obvious that there are some negotiations, and I can't explain the document because I didn't participate in the meeting. I cannot say on the basis of these documents that power had been taken over.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document consists of a number of pages. The Prosecutor is selecting two or three sentences, and on the basis of those sentences, asking the witness to give an answer. If we were to act correctly, then the witness should have time to read the whole document and only then answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that that is not the first time in this hall, Mr. Nobilo, that one or the other party is referring to passages from a document. The witness did not say what you said; he gave quite a different answer. But now I am going to ask the witness, does he wish to read the whole document? How many pages does this document have?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In B/C/S, Mr. President, it is seven pages single-spaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I think the witness is going to tell us: Do you wish to read the document in its entirety, Brigadier, or can you answer on the basis of the question put to you by the Prosecutor referring to certain passages, which appear to me to be quite clear but it is up to the witness to answer? Do you wish to study it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In order to be able to make proper conclusions regarding specific questions, I would like to read it. However, I too have an interest in proceeding rapidly, so it is up to Your Honour to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Brigadier, I asked you a question, and I just wish to draw your attention to the fact that if you wish to read the document, you will read it, but you will be staying much longer at the disposal of the Tribunal. You will not be able to return today, not even next week, to your offices. So if you wish to read the document, you can read it, and we will come back to that question later, Mr. Kehoe, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in order to speed up our work and to make my answers proper, I would like to read this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can he read it during the break, Mr. President? He can read it during the next break perhaps and we can save some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in agreement with my colleagues, proceed to your next question, and the General will read the whole document later on and provide an answer. I do wish to say that a part of the answer was given before the objection of Mr. Nobilo. So it was not the witness's request to read the whole document but Mr. Nobilo thought it would be better for his witness. So we will take note of that, and please go on to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, at the end of September of 1993, where were you working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the end of September, at the end of September, 1993, I was in the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I misspoke, Brigadier, I apologise. The end of September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the end of September 1992, I was working in the Defence department in Novi Travnik and appointed as Chief of Staff of the Civil Defence of the municipality, and in view of my expertise, I assisted in the establishment of HVO units in the town of Novi Travnik itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, the Defence department that you were working at in Novi Travnik in September of 1992, that was part of the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In September 1992 -- just a moment, please. Let me try and remember. The Defence department consisted of three premises, and there were both Croats and Muslims working in those premises. May I go on to the specific answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Brigadier. My question is: Was the Defence department that you were working for in September of 1992 part of the HVO; "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the HVO have 70 per cent of the power in Novi Travnik in September of 1992; "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are not being asked to answer exactly, you are being asked whether it was probably so or not, and I would like you to answer. You had a position where you were able to assess with a certain degree of probability.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, it is possible that that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I'm asking the witness a question, not the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, it is quite possible that that was so, because we saw it from the report of the president of the HVO. I can say that on the basis of that report and not on the basis of my personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So, it is possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, did the Bosnian Muslims in Central Bosnia resist the taking over of power by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer with a yes or no. Possibly they did resist, because we saw that there were certain incidents. I wasn't establishing that authority to be able to say yes or no; but it is possible, because there were certain incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 503, 503A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is a document that is dated 10 September, 1992 from the Vitez municipality, the coordination board for the protection of Muslim interests. If you could read the first paragraph, going into the second paragraph, it reads: "According to the decision of the so-called Croatian Defence Council government of Vitez Municipality, with a number -- INTERPRETER: A bit slower, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Of 3 September, 1992, it has been decided that instruction in elementary and secondary schools in the territory of the municipality of Vitez," some illegible words, "in 1992, the same decision states that schoolbooks published in the Republic of Croatia shall be used during instruction, and the school buildings and premises should be repaired in such a way that all emblems, pictures, frescos associated with the former Yugoslavia are removed." Next paragraph, first sentence. "We hereby voice our outrage at this decision, because it has been made by an illegal organ created by a principle of a single nationality." You're certainly welcome to read the rest of the document. Now, did that event take place in Novi Travnik, as well, i.e. the introduction of the Republic of Croatia curricula into the schools of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, as we move ahead, after, from September to October, and in Vitez; is it not true that in mid-October of 1992 the Vitezovi attacked the headquarters of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and drove them out of their headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it; but among the events that took place in Vitez in October, I'm aware only of an incident that occurred when the road was blocked at Grbavica and near Nadioci, between Nadioci and Ahmici at the cemetery. So I'm aware of that incident within this time period. As for the event you have referred to, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to Defence Exhibit 250, a document you identified and was received in evidence during your direct testimony. I direct your attention on the BCS version, to page 2, and it's also page 2 on the English version. It notes, does it not, that on the 15th of October, 1992, a battle team of eight soldiers sabotaged the headquarters of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? The commander of the team was Major Darko Kraljevic, and this is a report of the Vitezovi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is a report of the Vitezovi, and what you said is stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot assert that it did happen; but if the commander said it happened, then it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So, you would accept that on the 15th of October, 1992, the Vitezovi attacked the headquarters of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I accept what is written here in the way it was written in this report by the signatory, whose signature I recognise, that is, Dragan Vinac, deputy commander of the special purpose unit Vitezovi, Major Dragan Vinac. That is all I can confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, you're going to have the opportunity to read the document from the presidency about the take-over by the HVO in various municipalities; but my question, as opposed to focusing on that document, is a question: Was the HVO taking control in other parts of Bosnia, other than the municipalities that we have talked about here today? And were they driving the Muslims out of various areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether the HVO took over control in other municipalities. But as far as the take-over of power in Vitez, Busovaca and Novi Travnik, I cannot confirm that, because I know that there was a parallel Muslim authority. What form of authority it took, I do not know that. But I cannot confirm that the power was taken over in Busovaca, in Vitez or in Novi Travnik, even though the documents seem to say that the HVO apparently have different powers or government structure than the ones that used to exist before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, you just stated that, "I do not know whether the HVO took over control in other municipalities." In September and October --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- of 1992, you were working for the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in the HVO Travnik as a specialist for the organisation of units based on a volunteer list which I had available, and I was trying to organise units for the defence against the Serbs, and that was my principal task at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How far is Prozor from Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm going to try to tell you, approximately, about 90 kilometres, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 90 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could go to a video, and I have a particular -- the video has a talking role and it is in English. I have given copies of this, what we're about to play, to the translation booth so they can translate it into English, as well as translate into BCS. The video itself was a video that was played on TV in the United Kingdom known as Bosnia's Last Testament, and the narrator is s Vulliamy, an individual who testified before this Court in this Chamber, in this particular case. So, Your Honours, I can give you the particular transcript that I have previously given to the translators.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This video will be 504, and the report 504A, transcript, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could play the video? Could you back it up? Rewind it and raise the volume, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "This is Prozor, to the south of Travnik. One night in October I stopped for coffee in the busy main street. A few days later I returned to find Croatian mobs roaming through town and 5.000 Muslims driven into the mountains looking for caves in which to hide. The pillage and killing in Prozor was the start of a new Bosnian war and a bit of betrayal for the Muslims. This is the consolidation of a hard-line Croatian mini state within Bosnia calling itself Herceg-Bosna. This territory flies a Croatian flag, has a Croatian puppet government, uses Croatian money and even has special Croatian number plates, and it must say its rulers come under a Croatian army. Bosnians who refuse that authority are dealt with in the time honoured way."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can put the lights back up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, the events that we just reviewed, the ends of which took place in October of 1992, in Prozor, some 90 kilometres away from Novi Travnik. Are you aware of what happened to the Muslims in Prozor during the time period of September and October of 1992? Excuse me -- no, it was 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding the events in Prozor, I heard about them through the media. I know that there was a conflict, and what the results of that conflict were can be seen from this video clip. I have no doubt that it is authentic. I didn't go to Prozor before the war, and I passed through Prozor after the Washington Accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to clarify something. It is not quite clear to me, on the screen it said the 11th of April, 1993. My learned colleague said it was October 1992. In the transcript no mention of the year is made, but on the film we could see that it was April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The date on the actual film is 11 April, 1993, which is the date it ran on TV in the United Kingdom, and they date it from their filing system. The October that he is talking about is the, obviously, the previous year, October of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can clarify, Brigadier, that these events took place in Prozor in October of 1992; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that there was a conflict in October of 1992 in Prozor. I do not know the exact date, I do not know the causes, I do not know the participants, and if the consequences were such as are presented here; because I don't know, because I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, from what you do know, and what you learned about Prozor, and the events in October of 1992; were the Muslims driven out of Prozor by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the conflict took place, its consequences in Prozor, I don't know if it was 2.000 or 5.000, if the Muslim population withdrew from Prozor to some neighbouring towns, that is the consequence of this conflict. What the reasons are for the withdrawal, whether it was a consequence of combat operations, that I cannot speak to. I cannot say either way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention, again, to Vitez, where you were in Novi Travnik, and let us move ahead to November and discuss yet another document dated 26th of November, 1992. And, again, this is an SDA document, party of democratic action, which is the Muslim party, in Vitez, 26 November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 505, 505A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is a document, again, as I noted, dated 26 November, 1992, and it's a press release and reads as follows, and I will not read the entire matter. I will read the first two paragraphs, skip a paragraph, and go down to the fourth paragraph. But, of course, as always, you are welcome to read the entire document. "26 November, 1992. Press release. Since Wednesday, 25th of November, 1992, there has not been a single representative of the authorities of Muslim nationality in the building of the assembly of Vitez municipality. The Croatian Defence Council government of the municipality Vitez decided to ban, from the building of the assembly of Vitez municipality, all those who have not agreed to work within the system of the HVO government of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna. "For example, the president and one of the members of the Vitez municipal assembly, the president of the municipal misdemeanours court of Vitez, as well as some of the employees of the organs of administration, all of them Muslim nationality, have been prohibited from entering the building." Skip a paragraph. "We would like to point out that since 20 October, 1992, policemen of Muslim nationality have not been able to carry out their regular duties, only because they thought themselves to be an integral part of the police force of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and not in the service of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna." My first question for you, Brigadier, is: Do you know about these events of people being prevented from going to work for not coming under HVO authority, and for the police of Muslim ethnic nationality, not being able to do their work? Do you know about that in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These events, these specific incidents I'm not familiar with. I'm not familiar with what was going on with respect to the civilian authorities. But let me give you a general comment, an overall comment. All these documents about the establishment of the HVO authority which were compiled by the Muslim organisations was a result of the collapse of the central authorities. As you know, Sarajevo was already under siege, and everybody was organising themselves. As I pointed out earlier, they were taking over competencies of the central government, and I think that this can be seen in all these documents that we have been reviewing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You would agree with me, would you not, Brigadier, that the Bosnian Muslims believed they had no voice in the decisions of the HVO; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what rights were being offered in the HVO structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, during the same period of time, houses of prominent Muslims were being burned in the Vitez area; isn't that right? During this time frame, October and November time frame that we're talking about, Bosnian Muslim houses of prominent Bosnian Muslims were being burned; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not correct for this time period. I know that the consequence of the burning of houses was as a result of the armed conflicts. I am not aware of any incidents where houses were being burned outside of this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Outside the conflicts? Let me show you Defence Exhibit 347. Do you have that document before you, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was signed by General Blaskic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a document, Brigadier, that you identified in direct examination, and I believe that Judge Riad asked you a couple of questions about this. The note in line one, in point one, is that all measures shall be taken to prevent setting fire to houses of eminent citizens of Muslim nationality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The date of this document is 5 November, 1992; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, during the time frame that we're having these meetings in September, on the take-over of the municipalities, and during the time frame when Prozor is being burned and the Muslims are being driven out, Muslim houses in Vitez, houses of eminent Muslims are being burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Counsel knows full well this was sent to the HVO in Novi Travnik, not in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, that's closer to home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right in your backyard. That's better still. Houses of prominent Muslims are being burned in your municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. President, this is what I have to say regarding this document. This document was compiled on the basis of the agreement of General Merdan and Mr. Tihomir Blaskic and as a result of the cessation of hostilities between the HVO and the BH army, and it was within that conflict, which was in October, sometime around the 20th, that these houses were being burned. Muslim houses were not being set on fire, if there were no combat operations there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, in Novi Travnik municipality, your municipality, were the houses of eminent Bosnian Muslim citizens being torched and burned? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but only at the time of conflict. As far as I recall, during this conflict, one or two houses in the town of Novi Travnik were burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, the burning of these houses, in addition to the take-over of the HVO, in Novi Travnik, your municipality, and other municipalities, that that caused tension between the Bosnian Muslims and the Bosnian Croats in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
