utterances.text: Burning of houses, both Croatian and Bosnian, certainly contributed to the raising of tensions. In that respect, the answer is yes. However, the take-over of power, that is what I cannot agree with. I cannot, I don't agree that somebody took over power and the other side was completely outside of the power. I gave you the reasons why I believe that this power was then divided, that is, because of the collapse of the central government. You saw all the other problems that arose from this main collapse of central power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have you completed that point, Mr. Kehoe? We will take a break, if you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're going to take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Have the accused brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, we are going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We are going to move ahead from the fall and winter of 1992 to the events in January of 1993. My first question on this is: Did the people in the headquarters of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone know that a conflict was going to break out with the Bosnian Muslims, an armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please tell me the time frame with some precision when you are asking me whether we knew that there would be a conflict with the Muslims or, rather, the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, in the first week of January of 1993, was it the belief of the accused Colonel Blaskic and the other members of the headquarters, that a conflict was going to break out with the Bosnian Muslims and with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the conflict in January 1993 and according to our intelligence reports regarding the activities and intentions of the BH army, I personally did expect a conflict. My personal assessment was that there would be a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, maybe my question isn't clear, Brigadier. I'm saying to you that when you are in the headquarters in the first week of January in 1993, did you believe and did Colonel Blaskic believe that there was going to be a conflict with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, at that time, General Blaskic did not believe that a conflict could break out, but he always had a certain reservation as regards the possibility of such a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 506, 506A for the French version, 506B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, do you recognise Colonel Blaskic's signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do recognise it. This is Colonel Blaskic's signature, and it is the stamp of the Operative Zone Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let's just read this very briefly. It's 4 January, 1993, marked "Urgent." Time, 12.15. It's going to Central Bosnia Croatian Defence Council brigades, the anti-aircraft defence, and the artillery division, and there's deliveries in the lower left-hand corner to all the brigades. Preparatory language: "In order to draw up a plan of the tasks to be carried out by the Central Bosnian Operative Zone and to present a review of the state of engineering works --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have it in French, so to proceed more quickly, as we all have a copy, you could go on to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Unless it is very important for you to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's not, Mr. President. It just gives the witness a bit of a chance to review a document on the chance that he hasn't seen it before. I'm just trying to give him some opportunity to review it as well. But we will go straight to the questions and they deal with first the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 deals with an order by all brigades "to review the state of engineering works and territorial preparations." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And "engineering works" means, among other things, trenches, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular order is marked "Urgent" with a completion date of 10 January, 1993, for reports to be issued to the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next document, which is an order of the 7th of January, 1993. Mr. President, unfortunately, there is no French version for this one, so I will have to be pressed into the service of reading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The President has a wonderful command of English now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I am very pleased by what Judge Riad has said, but I still get on a little better with the French.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 507, 507A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, this is a document, appeared to be -- sending by packet, with the author looking to be like you, is it not? "S.M." in the lower left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, these are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure if that's the incoming stamp of you or the HVO Travnik, but I believe it's the incoming stamp of Travnik; right? If you don't know, you don't know. It's not important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be the packet stamp of Travnik. It says HVO Travnik. It could be. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, you wrote this, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the 7th of January, 1993, at 15.20, and let's read this order: The accused Colonel Blaskic issues an order to the Central Bosnian Operative Zone Brigades, to the HVO municipal authorities, as well as the Vitez Regional Military Police. This is a supplement to the order of 1419/92 of 5 December, 1992, and 1618/92 of 8 December, 1992. "Further to the need of harmonisation of working hours for hotel and catering establishments and the curfew in the zones of responsibility of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone, I hereby order: "1. Hotel and catering establishments may be open according to the following: "(a) In the municipalities of Travnik, Novi Travnik, Zepce, Usora until 1900 hours. In Vitez, in the Vitez municipality, until 2000 hours. In the municipalities of Busovaca, Kiseljak, Kresevo, Fojnica, Vares, Zenica, Kakanj until 2200 hours. "2. Curfew hours in the municipality of Novi Travnik, Zepce, Usora from 2000 hours until 0400 hours. In the Vitez municipality from 2100 hours until 0400 hours. In the municipalities of Busovaca, Kiseljak, Kresevo, Vares, Kakanj, Zenica from 2300 hours until 0400 hours. "This order goes into effect on 9 January, 1993, and the commander of the Military Police Battalion is responsible to me for its execution." Now, Brigadier, you wrote this document, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did write this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In this document, Colonel Blaskic is exercising command over civilian authorities, is he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be interpreted in that way on the basis of this order, but as I'm the author, let me explain the circumstances under which it was written. The document was issued because of repeated disturbances of public law and order, shooting around town, disturbing the peace, and then military men or military conscripts who had weapons would cause disorders in town, and the order was issued because the commander reached agreement with the civilian authorities, and it can be seen that he is giving it to the government for their information, not as an order, and the times were established as the civilian authorities wanted it, and since the civilian police -- I just explained the situation it was in at the time with inadequate arms and equipment, and it was not capable of carrying out military policing, so this assignment was given to the 4th Military Police Battalion and all its units within the territory of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. My conclusion: This document was designed to improve law and order for the citizens in the territory of this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, you just said that it can be seen that (Blaskic) is giving it to the government for their information, not as an order." But it's quite clear from this document, is it not, that Blaskic is giving an order to civilians that run hotel and catering establishments; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not right because I know how the document was drafted and what its role was. The times indicated were simply so that the Military Police would know what the working hours of various establishments were so that they could deal with problems together with the civilian police. The times were given by the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is an example of manipulation, and that is why I am objecting. I think the document needs to be read to the end. By partially reading the document, an attempt is made at manipulation. It says: "Deliver to the HVO governments for their information and to the brigades for execution," and if the document is read until the end, this becomes clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Please. Mr. President, I object to these comments about manipulation. The document speaks for itself. This is an order, not some permission that Blaskic is asking for; he's issuing an order to hotel establishments and catering establishments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Nobilo suggested that the document be read to the end. Would it be right to go to the top of the document and to see whether any assistance can be had from Order No. 1419 of 1992, unless you have already provided us with it. I don't know where it is. The writing there says that this order is a supplement to the Order No. 1419/92 of 5 December, 1992. Would that previous document be helpful in throwing light on some of the issues raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it would, Judge Shahabuddeen, but I don't think we have that. That's the problem. It would shed a tremendous amount of light on everything that is said in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Shahabuddeen. I would simply like to say to Mr. Nobilo, the word "manipulation," one must be very careful about using it, especially to the opposing party. Secondly, I think you are right. One should see the document in its entirety, but this is still an order sent for the sake of information. That's all. It is still an order sent for information purposes. So please be careful as regards your interpretations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do apologise if I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Kehoe, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your testimony, Brigadier, is that with the consent of the municipal authorities, Blaskic was given the power to give orders to civilian businesses as well as to civilians themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not saying that. I cannot assert that. In this specific case, one can see what has been ordered and I said on the basis of what this order was issued because I worked on it and I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, prior to this time, did you issue orders to hotels and catering establishments to give them the parameters of their working hours and did you send out orders on curfews, telling civilians what the curfews in the respective municipalities was going to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall specifically such orders, but I should like to try and recall the documents mentioned here by Judge Shahabuddeen. But I think that in this order, the times were changed. I can't be sure, but I think that in the previous orders, the times may have been different. It may have been 2000 hours, and then the municipalities probably thought that this was not appropriate, they asked for the times to be changed, and then we probably issued a new order indicating these new times. But I'm not 100 per cent sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, one last question on this document, Brigadier. You would agree with me that in setting out these hours, both the curfew hours and the business hours, Blaskic orders the 4th Military Police Battalion to ensure that people comply with this order; isn't that correct? And I am directing your attention to number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. By this order, the Military Police is assigned to carry out these duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This again is a document which there is no French translation yet, so unfortunately, I will have to read this document, which is one page over on to a little bit of the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 508, 508A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, what we have before us is an order from Brigadier Milvoj Petkovic; do you recognise that signature, or the stamp of Brigadier Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main headquarters of the HVO had such a stamp, and as far as I can recall, this could be General Petkovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's read this order that emanates Mostar on the 15th of January, 1993. It reads as follows: "On the basis of an order of the HVO Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, 01-1-32/93 of 15 January, 1993, of an order of the head of the defence department, 021/19 of 15 January, 1993, regarding the Geneva agreement on the arrangements for Bosnia-Herzegovina and the jurisdiction of the command of the armed forces in the provinces, I hereby issue the following order. 1. All units in the HVO and BH army, armed forces, in provinces 3, 8 and 10, the Croatian provinces, shall be placed under the command of the HVO main staff, i.e. under the command of the Central Bosnia north-west and south-east Herzegovina Operative Zone. 2. All HVO units in provinces 159, the Muslim provinces, shall be placed under the command of the BiH army staff, some of the brigades of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. 3. HVO forces in Kresevo and Kiseljak municipalities shall remain under the command of the HVO main staff, i.e. main staff, i.e. Central Bosnian Operative Zone until further notice. 4. Members and units of the HVO and BH army armed forces that fail to submit to the commands as stipulated in items 1 and 2 of this order must leave the territory of provinces they do not belong to, otherwise they will be considered paramilitary and disarmed. 5. Officers of the BH army shall be represented in the HVO armed forces commands at the Operative Zone and the brigade level, in proportion to the number of soldiers in the front. This follows the agreement on the joint commands. 6. BH army officers who, by their conduct, have contributed to disruption of relations between Croatian and Muslim nations shall not be members of the joint commands. 7. Operative Zone commanders shall start negotiating with BH army and find the best way of establishing joint commands. 8. The deadline for implementation of this order is 20 January, 1993. 9. A report on the implementation of this order shall be submitted to me every eight hours." Chief of the HVO main staff, Brigadier Milvoj Petkovic, and the copies go to the Operative Zone south-east, north-west Central Bosnia, 1st Mostar Brigade and files. Brigadier, do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, tell us about it, Brigadier, how did this come about? And tell us about what happened in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone when this order came into your possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the preamble, you see how it has come about. It is through HZHB, and it is pursuant to the negotiations in Geneva. I don't know what was decided there, but it had to do with organising the provinces, and I think that it regards the HVO as much as the BH army. I do not know what type of order the BH army main headquarters may have issued to their own units. As far as Central Bosnia Operative Zone is concerned, speaking operationally, we did not take any significant steps, I mean specifically. Although, I think that the commander may know more about the specifics of this document, but this is as much as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, focusing on paragraph one, you do know that province 10 is the area that covers basically the Lasva Valley area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this is so. I assume that it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on this order, and events around this time, is it your testimony that the Colonel Blaskic took no steps, based on this order, took no steps whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, because the task here is to establish contact with the BH army representatives. I do not know whether he, as the commander of the Operative Zone, established contact with the 3rd Corps commander or somebody at the equivalent level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there any other orders that came from Mostar on the 15th that would have caused Colonel Blaskic to take steps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall at this moment. If I was given a document, and I then I would maybe be able to refresh my memory. So, I cannot recall whether on that specific date that there was this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, you were in the headquarters at the time. Based on the decision to implement the Vance-Owen Plan in January, 15th of January, 1993, was it the belief within the headquarters that the HVO had to take some defensive measures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, sir. 456/6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could have the Brigadier also take a look at 508, I'm sorry, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Brigadier, the exhibit we just read, the order from Milvoj Petkovic, has a number of 0-70; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 01-70. Let's turn to this exhibit, which is an order of Colonel Blaskic. It refers to an order coming from the Mostar headquarters of 01/66, four orders prior to this implementation order for the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, my apologies, Mr. President, but there is no French version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But the date of the order is 16 January, 1993 at 1140 hours. And the title is, "Full combat readiness of all HVO formations in Central Bosnian Operative Zone. Order." And it goes to all formations in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, the Bruno Busic formation, Ludvig Pavlovic formation, the Vitezovi formation, Travnik police department, and the 4th Battalion of the military police. By the way the Travnik police department is a civil police structure; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Travnik police department was part of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that was the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Fine. Let's read it. "Pursuant to the order of the Mostar HVO headquarters, number 01-66/93, dated 15 January, 1993, and due to the open and deceitful aggression of Muslim forces all over the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, which has caused scores of HVO members to be killed and a number of them to be wounded, as well as Croatian homes to be burned and the Croatian people driven out, for the purpose of the self defence of the people and the territory of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, I hereby order the following: 1. Raise the combat readiness of HVO formations to the highest level. 2. All HVO formations are to be in a maximum state of readiness. All armed members of the Croatian people are to be included in the HVO formations. Cancel all leave and stop allowing people to go home, find accommodation for all HVO formations. Keep two shifts on duty along the front-line with the Chetniks and keep the other forces in full readiness for action against Muslim forces. All Muslims in the HVO formations who disobey our orders are to be disarmed and isolated. All weapons in private hands are to be collected in the logistics section of the brigades and used for arming men who are ready to fight. All Croatian villages are to be secured by sending in the necessary number of men, as assessed. 3. All brigades in the areas of conflict must have intervention units for mutual assistance. 4. HVO brigades, Jure Francetic from Zenica, and the Nikola Subic-Zrinski from Busovaca, are to organise monitoring of the stretch from Zenica and the area under the control of the Operative Zone. HVO Brigade Stjepan Tomasevic, from Novi Travnik, is to monitor the stretch towards Gornji Vakuf and be prepared to act if needed. 5. The 4th Military Police Battalion is to control the traffic and confiscate equipment and weapons of all Muslim transports and put them at the disposal of HVO forces. 6. 4th Military Police Battalion is to use its forces to secure the commands and HVO bodies. 7. I forbid members of the command to leave and go home for rest. 8. All persons and formations outside of our formations are not to be allowed into the zone of responsibility. 9. We are to prevent any individual or group in subordination. 10. All reports about the area and formations are to be handed to me and signed by the commanders themselves. 11. The deadline for readiness and compliance with this order is 18 January, 1993, at 0500 hours, with reports at 0600" -- excuse me, "0600 to 0630, at 1100 hours to 1130, at 1800 to 1830, at 2300 to 2330, and anything exceptional immediately, sentence as printed. 12. UNPROFOR humanitarian and transports are to be let through." And there is a delivery in the lower left-hand corner to any number of individuals, the brigades and the formations as we discussed. Now, my first question, Brigadier: Does that appear to be Colonel Blaskic's signature on the second page, and his stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is General Blaskic's signature, and the stamp is of the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was this order implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This order, such as was given here, was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, what was done and what was not done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to take it from item to item. Let me try to remember; because I did not remember the date of this document, but as I read through the contents, I recall the activities. I could not tell you individually what we did, what was implemented. I know there was no disarming of the BH army or the Muslim members of the HVO. I know that this did not happen. I do not know how the traffic control was conducted, that is, whether any convoy which was carrying stuff to the BH army was stopped and their goods confiscated. Regarding leave and everything else in that respect, we never had leaves, at least nobody in the Operative Zone command. Let me see about the mobilisation. Regarding the weapons which were in private possession, we were unable to collect it, because anything owned privately we were unable to collect. Later on, this was after Dayton, we were able to do so through SFOR. Let me read further. The intervention units and brigades we did not have. As far as I know, from this order, on the date when it was issued, there were no consequences, there was no conflict with respect to the implementation. I also want to add something else. It was issued through an order of the -- we were tasked ourselves by the Chief of Staff of the main headquarters, but whether these activities were necessary to be implemented in the larger areas of Orasje, south-eastern and north-western Herzegovina, that I do not know. But we did work on this order, and we sent it down to our subordinate units, but it had no effects. In other words, this order did not cause any conflicts on the 17th, 18th and following days. This is what I recall about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, you told us on direct examination that the conflict broke out in the Kacuni area at approximately the 24th of January; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that, and I also said why. I said what caused it. I think that there is a report from the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade on the killing of a policeman, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, the date I asked you for, excuse me for interrupting you, but we're coming down to the end of the day. You said it was the 24th of January. Yet approximately a week before Blaskic is ordering that two shifts be kept on the line against the Chetniks, the Bosnian Serbs, and the other forces should be moved into full readiness for action against the Muslim forces. Doesn't he order that on the 16th in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He also ordered that all Muslims and HVO formations should be disarmed. He says that, as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but those who disobeyed the HVO orders, because they were members of the HVO; so, who disobeyed the HVO orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say to disarm the Croats who disobey orders; does it? It points out the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not state that the Croats should be disarmed, it just states the disobeying orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On paragraph 5 he orders the military police to confiscate equipment and weapons from all Muslim transports and put them at the disposal of the HVO; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it states so here; and as far as I recall, this type of confiscation did not take place. Again, I repeat, this order was issued on the basis of another order by the Chief of Staff of the main headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, it sounds like he is getting ready for something; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This order is in the function of taking certain steps which would prevent any kind of surprise. As a professional soldier, this is how I interpreted this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Have you ever seen an order prior to this where Blaskic took units off the line against the Chetniks, told the Muslims to be disarmed, and then told the 4th Military Police Battalion to stop Muslim transports, to take weapons and equipment from them and put that weaponry and equipment at the disposal of the HVO? Is there another order like this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall another order. But, Mr. President, I would like to counter what the counsel is saying, because he keeps the same number of men against the Chetniks, except now we do not have three, but two shifts. Then, it does not state that the Muslims are to be disarmed. He only points out those who disobey the orders, so this is the correction I want to put in. And the rest is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm about to go into another area, if it would be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to take five minutes to have a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 25 (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 1.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of October, 1998 at 2.00 p.m. 25
